outcome: The full conjecture (every cubic bipartite 3-connected planar graph is Hamiltonian) remains open, but a genuine case of it was settled: a August 2025 preprint by Tobias Schnieders extends Goodey's 1975 special-case result (Hamiltonicity for face sizes up to 6) to face sizes up to 8, via a large computer-assisted case split (339,068,624 cases). This is not yet digested by experts (no journal acceptance or expert write-up found), so it is a settled-but-unreviewed case rather than an expert-confirmed one. A separate 2025 conference paper (Bekos, Kaufmann, Pfister, Graph Drawing 2025) improves a subhamiltonian-cycle bound (5n/6 edges vs. previous 2n/3) but explicitly does not address Hamiltonicity itself, so it is a related/weaker result rather than a case of the stated conjecture. No AI system was involved in either result.
summary: Barnette's conjecture (every cubic, bipartite, 3-connected planar graph is Hamiltonian) remains open as of September 2026; no proof or counterexample has been found. Within the 26 January 2024 window, two pieces of work surfaced. (1) Tobias Schnieders, 'Barnette Graphs with Faces up to Size 8 are Hamiltonian' (arXiv:2508.03531, submitted 5 August 2025), substantially strengthens Goodey's 1975 result (which proved Hamiltonicity when all faces have size ≤6) to graphs with faces of size ≤8, via a computer-assisted proof involving a case split of 339,068,624 cases. This is a genuine *case* of the stated conjecture under §3.1 (a restriction to a sub-class of Barnette graphs by face size), and settling it is progress in the confirming direction (more Barnette graphs shown Hamiltonian, none refuting the conjecture). It remains a preprint with no evidence of journal acceptance, expert digestion (no Tao/Quanta/survey coverage found), or independent verification of the computation, so I classify it `partial` rather than `resolved`. (2) Bekos, Kaufmann and Pfister, 'Approximating Barnette's Conjecture' (Graph Drawing 2025 / LIPIcs GD.2025.6), improves a bound on subhamiltonian cycles (book-embedding spine edges) from 2n/3 to 5n/6 in Barnette graphs, but the authors explicitly do not resolve or advance the Hamiltonicity question itself — this is a different (weaker, related) invariant, so it does not count as progress on the stated bullet and is mentioned only for context. Neither paper mentions any AI/ML system; the computational components are classical brute-force/case-enumeration methods, not AI. I also investigated 'ProofAtlas' (proofatlas.ai), a self-described 'AI-first formal mathematics' platform that lists Barnette's conjecture as one of ~198 open research programs it tracks. Its own page for Barnette's conjecture states the conjecture 'remains unresolved' with several named sub-problems (b=9 orbit list, b≥10 unbounded descent, tight-cut coordination, cycle merger) still open, and explicitly notes 'ProofAtlas has not executed or independently reproduced the current work attachments' — i.e., no claimed result, human- or AI-generated, exists there for this problem. ProofAtlas's own list of nine 'accepted' research advances (via a contributor called Lech Mazur, using Lean-checked proofs) does not include Barnette's conjecture at all — it covers Collatz, Sendov's conjecture, and several other unrelated problems. So while an AI-oriented research platform is actively organizing work on this exact conjecture as of August 2026, it has produced no finding, claim, or partial result on it to date; this is worth noting as an interesting near-miss for the AI question but is not itself an event to record.
competing_reading: One could argue the Schnieders face-size extension is 'incremental' enough, and insufficiently reviewed, to warrant `open` with the preprint merely noted rather than `partial`. I judge `partial` is correct because the rules state size is not the test and a case settled counts even via preprint — `partial` does not require expert digestion (only `resolved` does). A reader could also argue the Bekos et al. subhamiltonian-bound paper is itself a 'bound that moved' under `progress`/§3.1's related-problem carve-out, but since it is on a different invariant (book-embedding edge count, not existence of a Hamiltonian cycle) rather than a restriction of the stated question, I treat it as out of scope and mention it only in summary rather than making it the record's decisive event.
what_would_settle_it: Journal acceptance or an expert survey/blog digestion of the Schnieders preprint (or an independent re-verification of its case enumeration) would move that piece to `resolved`-level confidence for the face-≤8 case. Any future output from ProofAtlas or another AI system that produces a checked claim specifically on Barnette's conjecture (not just the currently unresolved research-program tracking) would be the first candidate for `ai_role` other than `none` on this problem.
